events.name: Re-Elect Laura Bellis: Pride-Season Celebration (Tulsa City Council, District 4)
events.description: City Councilor Laura Bellis throws a Pride-season party to keep District 4 in pro-equality hands, backed by a whole roster of community co-hosts. Suggested 27 dollars, a nod to the 27th anniversary of Tulsa's first Pride parade. RSVP for the address.
events.website_description: Laura Bellis is the kind of local leader who actually shows up for queer Tulsa, and this Pride-season celebration is your invitation to help keep her on the Tulsa City Council representing District Four. It is a warm, easy room full of community co-hosts, all there to support candidates committed to protecting human rights for every Tulsan. The suggested minimum donation is a sweet 27 dollars, honoring the 27th anniversary of Tulsa's first Pride parade, and the location is shared once you RSVP through the ActBlue link. Best-time tip for the shy ones: RSVP early so you get the address, then roll in right at 6 while the crowd is still small and easy to work, introduce yourself to one of the co-hosts, and you will have three new friends before the speeches even start. Showing up for an ally like this is one of the most useful nights you can give the community.

events.name: Rainbow Harvest: Free Farmers Market
events.venue: Dennis R. Neill Equality Center, 621 E 4th St
events.description: Free produce, zero judgment, and a whole lot of queer neighbors filling their tote bags at the Equality Center. Roll in between 1 and 4, grab what you need, and stay for the company. Pre-register so they know to expect you.
events.website_description: Rainbow Harvest is the Equality Center's free farmers market, and it is exactly the kind of low-key, big-hearted Saturday a shy introvert can actually handle. No cover, no pressure, just fresh groceries handed out from 1 to 4 PM and a crowd of LGBTQIA+ folks and allies who genuinely want you there. Pre-register at the form so the volunteers can pack enough for everyone, then show up, fill a bag, and let yourself be part of the neighborhood. Best-time tip: come right at 1 when the produce is fullest and the line is shortest, say hi to a volunteer, and you will leave with groceries and probably a new face you recognize next week.

events.name: Melanin Pride Yoga in the Park
events.description: Celebrate Pride in flow with KLASSIC's Melanin Pride Yoga in the Park, a Black queer outdoor session in the summer sun. Bring your own mat, they handle the water and snacks. Text or DM INFO to 918-888-6842 for the spot.
events.website_description: KLASSIC brings Black queer Tulsa a gorgeous way to mark Pride with Melanin Pride Yoga in the Park, an open-air flow built around community, melanin, and joy. Bring a mat and an open heart; water and snacks are provided, and the exact park location comes when you text or DM INFO to 918-888-6842. Best-time tip: message ahead for the location, arrive a few minutes early to claim a soft patch of grass, and let a morning of breath and sunshine set the tone for your whole weekend.

events.name: The Pride Era Drag Bingo
events.description: Oklahomans for Equality presents The Pride Era Drag Bingo with Porsche Lynn, Shanel Sterling, and Iman Scott. Doors at 2, show at 3, dab those cards and let the queens run the room. 18+ with ID.
events.website_description: Oklahomans for Equality turns bingo into a full drag spectacle with The Pride Era Drag Bingo at Bricktown Comedy Club, hosted by Porsche Lynn with Shanel Sterling and Iman Scott bringing the looks and the laughs. Doors open at 2 with the show at 3, and yes, you can actually win while the queens work the room. It is 18+ with valid ID, with premium front-row and general admission seating, and showroom guests grab at least two food or drink items. Best-time tip: buy online before prices jump at the door, get there near doors at 2 to snag a good table, and keep a dauber in each hand because these rounds move fast.

events.name: Queer Crafters Club
events.venue: Dennis R. Neill Equality Center, 621 E 4th St
events.description: Bring your half-finished cross-stitch, your glue gun, or absolutely nothing but yourself. Queer Crafters Club is two hours of making things and making friends, Thursday night at the Equality Center. Beginners and total chaos-crafters equally welcome.
events.website_description: Queer Crafters Club is the gentlest possible excuse to leave the house on a Thursday. From 6 to 8 PM at the Dennis R. Neill Equality Center, LGBTQIA+ crafters of every skill level gather to knit, paint, bead, glue, and gossip. You do not need to be good at anything, and you do not even need to bring a project, there is usually a spare set of supplies and a spare seat at the table. Best-time tip: walk in around 6 when folks are still setting up, claim a chair next to whoever looks friendliest, and let the small talk happen over a craft instead of forced eye contact. It recurs most Thursdays, so if this one sneaks up on you, there is always next week.
